subject.title: Model switch can fail silently when carried-over session context is too large

question: What should OpenClaw do when a persisted model switch or continuation would carry a session over the selected model's effective context budget?
rationale: Current code has enough budget metadata and multiple partial recovery paths, but choosing compact, warn, fail, fallback, or runtime-specific behavior affects provider routing, session state, replay safety, and documented overflow policy.

options.title: Shared budget check with recovery
options.body: Add a common switch/continuation budget check that auto-compacts when safe and otherwise gives explicit user-visible recovery guidance before or during the next run.

options.title: Warn only before switching
options.body: Keep model switching immediate but surface target-budget risk and recommend /compact or /new without automatically changing the session transcript.

options.title: Keep runtime-owned recovery
options.body: Document that overflow remains compaction/retry-owned after the next run starts, and improve diagnostics without adding a switch-time policy gate.

recommendation.title: Shared budget check with recovery
recommendation.body: Add a common switch/continuation budget check that auto-compacts when safe and otherwise gives explicit user-visible recovery guidance before or during the next run.

likelyOwner.reason: The live model-switch pending history and current product-policy boundary make Peter Steinberger the best available routing owner from the sampled history.
